findings.title: Windows fallback probe misses codemie.exe
findings.problem: Filter guards on lines 265 and 271 check d.join(&sidecar_name).exists() || d.join("codemie").exists(); the fallback probes for "codemie" without the .exe extension, which Rust's std::fs will not match against "codemie.exe" on Windows.
findings.impact: If the sidecar binary is placed as codemie.exe without the arch suffix, bin_dir resolves to None on Windows and PATH remains unchanged; reachability on the spike's macOS primary target is uncertain.
findings.recommendation: Add a #[cfg(target_os = "windows")]-guarded d.join("codemie.exe").exists() clause to the fallback condition on both lines 265 and 271, or unify into a platform-aware probe helper.

findings.title: Unset PATH yields trailing separator — CWD implicit in PATH
findings.problem: Line 274 uses env::var("PATH").unwrap_or_default(); if PATH is unset this returns ""; line 276 then produces "<dir>:" with a trailing colon, which POSIX shells interpret as an implicit '.' (CWD) entry in PATH.
findings.impact: Any executable in the working directory at app launch time can shadow searched commands; the attack surface is an attacker-controlled file in a writable CWD.
findings.recommendation: Guard the format call to omit the separator when current is empty: format!("{}{}{}", dir.display(), if current.is_empty() { "" } else { ":" }, current), or reuse the existing PATH_SEP pattern from add_to_path.

findings.title: Unsafe set_var called after log plugin install
findings.problem: lib.rs installs tauri_plugin_log at lines 14-18 (debug builds only) before calling inject_bundled_bin_path at line 23; the SAFETY comment asserts no thread is spawned, which may be false if the log plugin starts a background thread during install; concurrent getenv and set_var is UB in Rust.
findings.impact: On debug builds, process state may be silently corrupted or a SIGSEGV produced; reachability is uncertain without confirming tauri_plugin_log's thread behaviour during plugin().
findings.recommendation: Move the inject_bundled_bin_path call before any plugin is installed, or replace the SAFETY comment with a verified reference to tauri_plugin_log's documented thread behaviour (e.g. no background thread before the first log call).

findings.title: Hardcoded colon separator ignores PATH_SEP
findings.problem: inject_bundled_bin_path constructs PATH as format!("{}:{}", dir.display(), current), hardcoding ':' regardless of OS; pathman.rs defines PATH_SEP as ';' on Windows and ':' elsewhere — the new function ignores it.
findings.impact: On Windows builds PATH is written with ':' separators, rendering it malformed and preventing the sidecar from being found; the spec criterion for platform-specific separator (Spec Phase 3 Rust) is explicitly unmet.
findings.recommendation: Replace the ':' literal with the existing PATH_SEP constant: format!("{}{}{}", dir.display(), PATH_SEP, current).

findings.title: Non-UTF-8 path bytes silently replaced in PATH entry
findings.problem: dir.display() uses to_string_lossy() internally; on filesystems that permit non-UTF-8 path components the bin_dir entry written to PATH will contain Unicode replacement characters (U+FFFD), making the directory silently unreachable.
findings.impact: Uncertain reachability on macOS (HFS+/APFS enforce UTF-8); on Linux or legacy volumes the sidecar is unreachable despite PATH appearing to be set.
findings.recommendation: After constructing the PATH string, verify dir.to_str() returns Some; if None, log a warning and skip injection rather than silently writing a corrupted PATH entry.

findings.title: Sidecar not found logged but not surfaced to user
findings.problem: When both current_exe and resource_dir probes fail, the else branch at line 278-280 emits a log::warn! only; inject_bundled_bin_path returns () and lib.rs line 23 discards the result; no user-visible error is produced.
findings.impact: All codemie invocations fail silently with 'command not found'; the user cannot distinguish a broken installation from a missing sidecar.
findings.recommendation: Return Result<(), String> from inject_bundled_bin_path, propagate through setup(), and surface the failure as a visible dialog or structured error entry in the installer log.

findings.title: Required spike config file absent from diff
findings.problem: The spec requires src-tauri/tauri.macos.conf.json with externalBin: ["../assets/bin/codemie"], bundle.macOS.signingIdentity, and [throwaway] comments on every spike-specific key; the file does not appear in the diff.
findings.impact: Story criterion AC5 is unmet; the spike cannot be built or run in its intended signed/notarized form without the platform-specific Tauri configuration.
findings.recommendation: Create src-tauri/tauri.macos.conf.json with the keys specified in the spike plan, add [throwaway] comments on each spike-specific key, and reference it in the Tauri build invocation.

findings.title: System Node probe not bypassed for bundled binary
findings.problem: ui/handlers.js lines 109-149 (step 1.2 — the system Node check and download step) are unmodified; the spec requires short-circuiting this step when the bundled binary path is in use.
findings.impact: Spec criterion Phase 3 JS (step 1.2) is unmet; the bundled binary install flow will trigger an unnecessary and potentially failing system Node probe.
findings.recommendation: Add a guard at the top of the '1.2' handler to return true immediately when the PATH-injected codemie binary is detected, bypassing the Node check and download entirely.

findings.title: npm install not replaced with codemie --version probe
findings.problem: ui/handlers.js line 175 still invokes npm install -g @codemieai/code; the spec requires replacing step 1.3 with a codemie --version probe against the PATH-injected binary.
findings.impact: Spec criterion Phase 3 JS (step 1.3) is unmet; the install flow will attempt a global npm install instead of validating the bundled binary.
findings.recommendation: Replace the npm install -g @codemieai/code invocation at line 175 with a codemie --version probe and treat exit code 0 as the success criterion.

findings.title: '[throwaway]' prefix violates documented commit format
findings.problem: git-workflow.md documents commit format as '<type>: <short description>' with no prefix; all 5 commits in range use '[throwaway] <type>: <description>'; the branch name 'spike/EPMCDME-14504-pkg-binary' also does not match any documented prefix pattern.
findings.impact: Non-conformant commit subjects violate the documented history convention; under squash-merge the prefix would carry into the main-branch record.
findings.recommendation: Rebase to drop the '[throwaway]' prefix from all 5 commit subjects so each reads '<type>: <short description>'; also rename the branch to a documented prefix (e.g. feat/EPMCDME-14504-pkg-binary) before merge.
